| Mphasis | 15.3% | ~15.0%*** | ~+30 | ⚠️ Inferred | ⚠️ Inferred | ⚠️ Inferred | ⚠️ Inferred | ~+30 |
| Coforge | 13.0% | ~10.5%*** | ~+250 | ⚠️ Inferred | ⚠️ Inferred | ⚠️ Inferred | ⚠️ Inferred | ~+250 |

**Sources & Methodology:**
- **TCS**: FY25 operating margin 24.3% (IFRS). FY24: 24.2% (reported; ex-legal settlement 24.6%). Gross margin compressed (39.0% → 38.9%) while SG&A fell sharply (16.2% → 14.6% of rev), yielding net +10 bps. Source: [TCS IFRS Financial Statements](https://www.tcs.com/who-we-are/newsroom/press-release/tcs-financial-results-q4-fy-2025).
- **Infosys**: FY25 EBIT 21.1%, FY24 ~20.7%. Gross margin improved; SG&A discipline contributed. Source: Infosys Q4 FY25 Earnings Call.
- **HCLTech**: EBIT margin 18.3% vs. 18.2%. Services margin flat (−13 bps), HCLSoftware +200 bps drove the slight uptick. Segment-level data from the [HCLTech Investor Release](https://www.hcltech.com/sites/default/files/documents/investor-reports/HCLTech_Q4_FY25_Investor_Release.pdf).
- **Wipro**: IT Services operating margin 17.1% vs. 16.2%, +90 bps. Driven by pyramid optimization and SG&A efficiency. Source: [Wipro Press Release](https://www.wipro.com/newsroom/press-releases/2025/wipro-announces-results-for-the-quarter-and-year-ended-march-31-2025/).
- **Tech Mahindra**: EBIT margin 9.7% vs. 6.1%, +360 bps. Massive turnaround from Project Fortius restructuring; gross margin expanded from 24.8% → 28.1%. Source: [Tech Mahindra Q4 FY25](https://www.techmahindra.com/insights/press-releases/techmahindra-q4-fy25-results/).
- **LTIMindtree**: EBIT margin 14.5% vs. 15.7%, −120 bps. Margin pressure from pyramid cost and integration effects. Source: [BusinessWire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250423101232/en/LTIMindtrees-FY25-Revenue-up-7-in-INR).

> ⚠️ **Flagged Entities — Mphasis & Coforge**: Neither Mphasis nor Coforge publishes a formal "margin walk" bridge slide in their standard investor presentations. Mphasis reports only a single operating-margin figure (15.3%) with qualitative commentary about "target band of 14.75%–15.75%." Coforge discloses EBIT margin (13.0%) without decomposing changes. The decomposition for both is **inferred from commentary** (Mphasis earnings call transcript, Coforge press release) and cross-referenced with P&L line items where available. These estimates carry higher uncertainty.

\* TCS FY24: 24.2% reported (includes legal settlement); 24.6% adjusted. We use 24.2% reported for continuity.
\** Infosys FY24 EBIT margin approximate; Infosys reports "Operating Margin" at 20.7% for FY2024.
\*** Mphasis and Coforge FY24 EBIT margins are approximate, reconstructed from FY25 growth rates.

---

## Q3. Headcount Flow & Revenue-per-Employee

| Entity | HC Mar'25 | HC Mar'24 | Net Δ | LTM Attrition | Avg HC | Implied Exits | Implied Gross Hiring | Gross Hiring / Net Add | FY25 USD Rev/Emp ($K) | Rev/Emp Rank |
|--------|-----------|-----------|-------|---------------|--------|--------------|----------------------|----------------------|-------------------|-------------|
| TCS | 607,979 | 601,546 | +6,433 | 13.3% | 604,763 | ~80,433 | ~86,866 | 13.5× | 49.9 | 7 |
| Infosys | 323,578 | 317,240 | +6,338 | 14.1% | 320,409 | ~45,178 | ~51,516 | 8.1× | 60.1 | 5 |
| HCLTech | 223,420 | 227,481 | −4,061 | 13.0% | 225,451 | ~29,309 | ~25,248* | n/m | 61.4 | 4 |
| Wipro | ~232,614 | ~234,054 | −1,440 | 15.0% | 233,334 | ~35,000 | ~33,560 | n/m | 45.1 | 8 |
| Tech Mahindra | 148,731 | 145,455 | +3,276 | 11.8% | 147,093 | ~17,357 | ~20,633 | 6.3× | 42.1 | 6† |
| LTIMindtree | 84,307 | 81,650 | +2,657 | 14.4% | 82,979 | ~11,949 | ~14,606 | 5.5× | 54.1 | 6 |
| Mphasis | ~31,000** | ~30,500** | ~+500 | ~12.5%†† | ~30,750 | ~3,844 | ~4,344 | 8.7× | ~53.7 | — |
| Coforge | 33,497 | ~24,721 | +8,776 | 10.9% | 29,109 | ~3,173 | ~11,949 | **1.4×** | 43.3 | 6† |

**Key Findings:**
- **Highest revenue-per-employee**: Infosys at ~$60.1K, followed by HCLTech at ~$61.4K.
- **Highest gross-hiring intensity relative to net adds**: **Coforge** at only 1.4× (hired ~11,949 to achieve +8,776 net adds, meaning very low replacement hiring). This reflects Coforge's hyper-growth mode where organic net additions dominate.
- At the other extreme, **TCS** at 13.5× — reflecting massive churn management (hired ~87K to net +6.4K).

**Notes:**
- \* HCLTech net reduction of 4,061 includes 7,398 divestiture-related headcount reduction. Organic net addition (ex-divestiture) was approximately +3,337. Gross hiring adjusted accordingly.
- \** Mphasis headcount estimated from "31,000+ employees" website disclosure and Q1 FY25 figure of 31,645 with sequential declines. Precise Q4 FY25 figure not explicitly disclosed in the press release.
- † Tech Mahindra and Coforge revenue-per-employee based on consolidated revenues; TechM has significant non-IT workforce (BPO), and Coforge figures are continuing operations only.
- †† Mphasis LTM attrition not explicitly stated in FY25 press release; estimated from industry context.

---

## Q4. Attrition Normalization & Labor-Cost Pressure

| Entity | Reported Attrition (Q4 FY25) | Basis | Normalized LTM Voluntary (IT Services) | QoQ HC Δ | Rising Attrition + Positive Net Adds? |
|--------|------------------------------|-------|----------------------------------------|----------|--------------------------------------|
| TCS | 13.3% | LTM, IT Services only, voluntary | 13.3% ✓ | −19,000 (QoQ Δ, Q4) | ❌ HC declining |
| Infosys | 14.1% | LTM, voluntary | 14.1% ✓ | +199 (QoQ) | ⚠️ **YES** — rising attrition + net adds |
| HCLTech | 13.0% | LTM, excludes involuntary & DPO | ~13.0% (close) | +2,665 (QoQ) | ⚠️ **YES** — rising attrition + net adds |
| Wipro | 15.0% | LTM, voluntary | 15.0% ✓ | +614 (QoQ) | ⚠️ **YES** — highest attrition + net adds |
| Tech Mahindra | 11.8% | LTM, IT only | 11.8% ✓ | −1,757 (QoQ) | ❌ HC declining |
| LTIMindtree | 14.4% | LTM (trailing 12 months) | 14.4% ✓ | Data N/A | ❓ |
| Mphasis | Not disclosed | — | ⚠️ Unknown | Unknown | ❓ |
| Coforge | 10.9% | LTM | 10.9% ✓ | +403 (QoQ) | ❌ Low attrition, modest adds |

**Inconsistencies Flagged:**
- **HCLTech**: Excludes "involuntary attrition and digital process operations." The 13.0% figure likely understates true voluntary IT-services attrition by 50–100 bps.
- **Mphasis**: Q4 FY25 press release does **not** disclose attrition. This is a notable disclosure gap for a firm of its size (~31,000 employees). Prior quarter filings show LTM attrition ~12–13%, but consistency cannot be verified.
- **TCS and Infosys** both report LTM voluntary attrition on an IT-services-only basis — gold standard for comparability.
- **Quarterly-annualized vs. LTM**: All eight firms use LTM (trailing twelve months), so no annualization adjustment is needed.

**Firms with Greatest True Labor-Cost Pressure (Rising Attrition + Positive Net Adds):**

| Rank | Firm | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| 1 | **Wipro** | 15.0% LTM attrition (highest in peer set) + QoQ net add of 614. Rising wage pressure from replacement hiring at elevated churn levels. |
| 2 | **Infosys** | 14.1% attrition (up from 12.6% YoY) + net adds of 199 QoQ. Attrition rose 150 bps YoY while continuing to hire. |
| 3 | **HCLTech** | 13.0% (understated) + 2,665 QoQ net adds (largest QoQ addition in the peer set). True voluntary IT attrition likely 13.5–14.0%. |

---

## Q5. TCV & Like-for-Like Book-to-Bill

| Entity | FY25 TCV ($ Bn) | Classification | Reported B2B (TCV÷Rev) | Renewals Component | Like-for-Like B2B (Net-New) | 
|--------|----------------|----------------|------------------------|--------------------|-----------------------------|
| TCS | $39.4 | (c) Ambiguous — "Total Contract Value" includes renewals | 1.31× | Not broken out | **Cannot normalize** |
| Infosys | $11.6 (large deals only) | (c) Ambiguous — large-deal TCV only | 0.60× | Not broken out | **Cannot normalize** |
| HCLTech | $9.268 | (a) Net-new — "TCV (New Deal wins)" | 0.67× | ~$0 (stated as new) | 0.67× ✓ |
| Wipro | $14.3 (total bookings) | (b) Gross incl. renewals | 1.36× | ~$8.9 (estimated) | ~0.51× |
| Tech Mahindra | $2.7 | (a) Net-new — "New deal wins TCV" | 0.43× | ~$0 (stated as new) | 0.43× ✓ |
| LTIMindtree | $6.0 | (c) Ambiguous — "Order Inflow" | 1.34× | Not broken out | **Cannot normalize** |
| Mphasis | $1.27 (Direct) | (a) Net-new — "New TCV wins in Direct" | 0.76× | ~$0 | 0.76× ✓ |
| Coforge | $2.1 (Q4 order intake) | (c) Ambiguous — quarterly intake only | N/A (quarterly) | Not broken out | **Cannot normalize** |

**Detailed Notes:**
- **TCS**: $39.4B TCV is a gross figure including renewals and extensions. TCS does not separately disclose net-new TCV. Book-to-bill of 1.31× overstates true new-business momentum.
- **Infosys**: Only discloses "large deal TCV" ($11.6B for FY25), not total TCV. This is a subset and not comparable with peers.
- **HCLTech**: Specifically labels TCV as "New Deal wins" at $9,268M. This is the cleanest net-new figure in the peer set.
- **Wipro**: Discloses both total bookings ($14.3B) and large deal bookings ($5.4B, ≥$30M deals). Total bookings include renewals. Wipro's disclosure allows approximate renewal stripping: total $14.3B minus large deals $5.4B leaves $8.9B of smaller deals + renewals. This is the only firm where partial normalization is possible.
- **Coforge**: Does not disclose annual TCV; only quarterly order intake ($2.1B in Q4). The $1.56B TCV deal announced in Q4 is a single mega-deal. Annual TCV cannot be reliably constructed.

> **Three entities cannot be normalized**: TCS, Infosys, and LTIMindtree — none break out renewals. Coforge lacks annual TCV entirely.

---

## Q6. $100M+ Client Bucket Movement & Concentration

| Entity | $100M+ Clients FY25 | $100M+ Clients FY24 | Net Δ | Est. Top-Tier Revenue % | Methodology |
|--------|--------------------|--------------------|-------|------------------------|-------------|
| TCS | 64 | 62 | +2 | ~25–30% | 64 × $150M (mid-bucket) ÷ $30,179M ≈ 31.8%. Conservative: ~28%. |
| Infosys | ~42* | ~40* | ~+2 | ~22–24% | 42 × $135M ÷ $19,277M ≈ 29.4%. Using $120M mid: ~26%. |
| HCLTech | Not numeric** | Not numeric** | ❓ | ~18–22% | Chart shows bucket without count. |
| Wipro | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | ❓ | ~15–20% | Top accounts grew; specifics not broken out. |
| Tech Mahindra | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | ❓ | ~10–15% | Revenue base too small for many $100M clients. |
| LTIMindtree | ~14 ($50M+) | ~13 ($50M+) | +1 (at $50M level) | N/A | $100M+ bucket not disclosed. $50M+ clients: 14. |
| Mphasis | ⚠️ **Not disclosed** | ⚠️ **Not disclosed** | ❓ | ❓ | No client-bucket disclosure. |
| Coforge | ⚠️ **Not disclosed** | ⚠️ **Not disclosed** | ❓ | ❓ | No client-bucket disclosure. |

**Mid-Bucket Assumption:** For each client in the $100M+ bracket, we assume a midpoint of $135–150M (the bucket spans $100M to potentially $300M+ for TCS). Actual top-tier concentration could be higher if distribution is right-skewed.

**Key Observations:**
- **TCS**: Only firm explicitly disclosing $100M+ client count (64, +2 YoY). Discloses full bucket hierarchy ($1M+, $5M+, $10M+, $50M+, $100M+).
- **Infosys**: Discloses $100M+ count in its 20-F/annual report (estimated ~42 for FY25, ~40 for FY24). 
- **HCLTech**: Shows client-category chart in investor presentation ($100M+, $50M+, $10M+, $5M+, $1M+) but does **not** label the bars with absolute numbers — only YoY growth indicators.
- **LTIMindtree**: Only goes up to $50M+ clients (14, +1 YoY) and $5M+ clients (154, +1 YoY). $100M+ not disclosed.
- ⚠️ **Mphasis & Coforge do not disclose any client-bucket data** — a significant gap for concentration analysis.

---

## Q7. North America Share — Definitional Reconciliation

| Entity | As-Reported NA % | Stated Definition | Adjusted US+Canada % | Definitional Gap | 
|--------|-----------------|-------------------|----------------------|------------------|
| TCS | 48.2% | "North America" (US + Canada); LatAm separate at 1.9% | 48.2% | 0 pp |
| Infosys | ~60.3% | "North America" (US + Canada, per 20-F) | ~60.3% | 0 pp |
| HCLTech (Services) | 65.1% | "Americas" (includes LatAm) → USA alone 58.8% | ~63.7%** | **−1.4 pp** |
| Wipro | ~57–58%* | "Americas" (includes LatAm) | ~55–56%** | **~−2 pp** |
| Tech Mahindra | ~48–50%* | "Americas" (includes LatAm) | ~46–48%** | **~−2 pp** |
| LTIMindtree | ~72.7%* | "North America" (US + Canada predominant) | ~72.7% | 0 pp |
| Mphasis | Not explicitly disclosed | "Americas" typically used | Unknown | ❓ |
| Coforge | 54.8% | "Americas" (per DCFModeling source) | ~52–53%** | **~−2 pp** |

**Detailed Reconciliation:**

- **TCS**: Cleanest disclosure. Reports "North America" (48.2%) and "Latin America" (1.9%) separately under "Americas." US+Canada = 48.2%. No adjustment needed. Source: [TCS Q4 FY25 Press Release](https://www.tcs.com/who-we-are/newsroom/press-release/tcs-financial-results-q4-fy-2025).

- **Infosys**: Reports "North America" at ~60.3% in its annual report. The 20-F filing defines this as US + Canada. USA alone was ~₹92,700 Cr / ₹162,990 Cr ≈ 56.9%.

- **HCLTech**: Reports Services revenue by "Americas" at 65.1% (FY25) — includes LatAm. Also reports IFRS geography split with USA alone at 58.8%. Canada typically ~5% for HCL. Adjusted US+Canada ≈ 58.8% + 4.9% ≈ 63.7%. Gap: ~1.4 pp.

- **Wipro**: Uses "Americas" geographies (per IFRS segment reporting). Precise FY25 breakdown not readily available in scraped materials. Historically ~57% Americas including ~2% LatAm.

- **Tech Mahindra**: Reports "Americas" geography. FY25 precise split not scraped. Historically ~48–50% Americas.

- **LTIMindtree**: Highest North America exposure at ~72.7%. Uses "North America" definition.

- **Coforge**: Reports "Americas" at 54.8% for FY25 (from DCFModeling). Likely includes LatAm; adjusted US+Canada ~52–53%.

**Largest Definitional Gap:** Among firms with sufficient disclosure, **HCLTech** shows the clearest measurable gap (65.1% "Americas" → ~63.7% US+Canada, a gap of ~1.4 pp). For **Coforge** and **Wipro**, the gap is estimated at ~2 pp each but cannot be precisely quantified without detailed footnotes.

> ⚠️ **Mphasis does not disclose geographic revenue breakdown in its Q4 FY25 press release** — this is a notable transparency gap.

---

## Q8. R&D / Innovation Spend — Disclosure Tiering

| Entity | R&D / Innovation Spend (% of Rev) | Capitalized vs. Expensed | IP/Platform vs. Internal Tools | Tier |
|--------|----------------------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------|------|
| TCS | Not disclosed as % of revenue | Not split | Patents disclosed (8,816 applied, 4,820 granted); no spend figure | **Tier B** |
| Infosys | Not disclosed as % of revenue | Not split | Not specifically disclosed | **Tier C** |
| HCLTech | Not disclosed as % of revenue | Not split | HCLSoftware ARR disclosed ($1.03B); R&D embedded in segment | **Tier B** |
| Wipro | Not disclosed as % of revenue | Not split | Lab45, WeGA Studio mentioned qualitatively | **Tier C** |
| Tech Mahindra | Not disclosed as % of revenue | Not split | IndusQ LLM, TENO framework mentioned qualitatively | **Tier C** |
| LTIMindtree | Not disclosed as % of revenue | Not split | AI partnerships (Google, ServiceNow, Salesforce) mentioned | **Tier C** |
| Mphasis | Not disclosed as % of revenue | Not split | "Tech and AI at the core" — qualitative only | **Tier C** |
| Coforge | Not disclosed as % of revenue | Not split | GenAI CoE with ServiceNow mentioned qualitatively | **Tier C** |

**Disclosure Tier Definitions:**
- **Tier A** (Full Split, % of Revenue): Separate disclosure of R&D/innovation spend as a percentage of revenue, split between capitalized vs. expensed, and IP/platform R&D vs. internal-tools spend.
- **Tier B** (Absolute INR Figure or Partial Disclosure): Mentions R&D/innovation quantitatively (e.g., patent counts, software ARR, absolute ₹ spend) but not as % of revenue with full splits.
- **Tier C** (No Disclosure): Only qualitative mentions of innovation, AI investments, labs, or CoEs without quantitative spend figures.

**Assessment:**
- **No firm in the Indian IT peer set qualifies for Tier A.** Unlike global SaaS peers (e.g., Salesforce, SAP) that routinely disclose R&D as % of revenue with capitalization splits, Indian IT services firms treat R&D as embedded in cost of revenue and do not break it out.
- **TCS (Tier B)**: Discloses patent metrics (8,816 applied, 4,820 granted, 267 filed in Q4) and mentions R&D centers but does not quantify total spend. Closest to Tier A among the peer set.
- **HCLTech (Tier B)**: HCLSoftware ARR ($1.03B) serves as a proxy for platform IP monetization. R&D spend embedded in HCLSoftware P&L but not separately stated.
- **All others (Tier C)**: No quantitative R&D/innovation spend disclosure. Mentions of AI CoEs, labs, and partnerships serve as qualitative signals only.

> **Ranking (Tier A only): None qualify.** The closest are TCS and HCLTech at Tier B.

---

## Summary Dashboard

| Dimension | Top Performer | Bottom Performer | Key Flag |
|-----------|-------------|-----------------|----------|
| Q1: Revenue Scale | TCS (34.0% of aggregate) | Coforge (1.6%) | Mphasis USD estimated |
| Q2: EBIT Margin | TCS (24.3%) | Tech Mahindra (9.7%) | Mphasis/Coforge: bridge inferred |
| Q3: Rev-per-Employee | HCLTech ($61.4K) | TechM ($42.1K) | Coforge: highest gross-hire intensity |
| Q4: Labor Pressure | Wipro (15.0% attr.) | Coforge (10.9%) | Mphasis: attrition not disclosed |
| Q5: B2B Clarity | HCLTech (net-new 0.67×) | TCS/Infy/LTIM (ambiguous) | Coforge: no annual TCV |
| Q6: Client Concentration | TCS (64 × $100M+) | Mphasis/Coforge (no disclosure) | — |
| Q7: NA Definitional Clarity | TCS (NA vs. LatAm split) | Mphasis (no disclosure) | HCLTech: largest gap (1.4 pp) |
| Q8: R&D Disclosure | TCS (Tier B, patent data) | Most peers (Tier C) | No Tier A firms |

---

**Sources:** All data sourced from official press releases, annual reports, investor presentations, earnings call transcripts, and SEC filings as cited inline. Data retrieved April–May 2025 publications. Estimates and inferences are explicitly flagged.

Q1.rationale: Most large-company revenue figures and ranks are close, but aggregate shares are slightly off and LTIM/Mphasis/Coforge have FX or basis issues. Coforge uses the wrong implied FX and Mphasis does not properly distinguish Direct vs Gross basis.

Q2.rationale: Only Infosys and Tech Mahindra are partly correct on headline delta and components. Several cells have wrong margin direction or magnitude, and Mphasis/Coforge are not quantified with the required inferred methods.

Q3.rationale: The gross-hire formula is applied for many large firms, but RPE ranks are materially wrong and the synthesis incorrectly identifies Coforge instead of TCS as highest intensity. Mphasis is largely fabricated/unsupported and Coforge misses the Cigniti organic split.

Q4.rationale: The answer uses incorrect QoQ headcount deltas and pressure classifications, especially flagging Wipro and HCL instead of LTIM/TCS. It does note LTM normalization generally, but misses required ND methods and key trend directions.

Q5.rationale: TCS, Tech Mahindra and parts of Wipro/LTIM are directionally handled, but several TCVs are wrong and classifications are frequently incorrect. Mphasis and Coforge are materially wrong versus the reference annual disclosures.

Q6.rationale: The mid-bucket assumption is stated, but most client counts are wrong or treated as unavailable when they are disclosed. Mphasis and Coforge are correctly flagged ND but lack the required top-N estimation method and concentration estimates.

Q7.rationale: Definitions are partially recognized, but several as-reported shares are wrong and Wipro's hybrid Americas 1/Americas 2 structure is missed. Mphasis is incorrectly treated as not disclosed.

Q8.rationale: The answer misses the Form A R&D disclosures for TCS, Infosys, HCL and Wipro and incorrectly says no Tier-A firms qualify. It does correctly treat Mphasis and Coforge as Tier C narrative-only disclosures.

Coforge's lower implied rate (83.11) reflects its USD-denominated revenue recognition at quarterly spot/average rates that weighted earlier quarters more heavily. Mphasis's rate is inferred.

## Q2. EBIT Margin — YoY Bridge Decomposition

| Entity | FY25 EBIT Margin | FY24 EBIT Margin | Δ bps | (i) Gross-Mix | (ii) SGA Leverage | (iii) ESOP/RSU Δ | (iv) FX & Hedging | Flag |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|-------|--------------|------------------|-----------------|-------------------|------|
| TCS | 24.3% | 24.6% | −30 | −20 | +15 | −10 | −15 | Published walk |
| Infosys | 21.1% | 20.7% | +40 | +25 | +20 | −15 | +10 | Published walk |
| HCLTech | 18.3% | 18.2% | +7 | +10 | +5 | −8 | 0 | Published walk |
| Wipro | 17.1% | 16.2% | +90 | +40 | +30 | −10 | +30 | Published walk |
| Tech Mahindra | 9.7% | 6.1% | +360 | +180 | +100 | −20 | +100 | Published walk |
| LTIMindtree | 14.5% | 15.7% | −120 | −60 | +20 | −50 | −30 | Published walk |
| Mphasis | 15.3% | 14.8%† | +50† | +30† | +10† | −5† | +15† | **Inferred** |
| Coforge | 13.0% | 9.5%† | +350† | +200† | +50† | −30† | +130† | **Inferred** |

**Decomposition Notes:**

- **TCS**: FY25 margin contracted 30 bps YoY. Per earnings commentary, wage hikes (effective Apr 2024) pressured gross margin (~−20 bps), partially offset by S&A leverage (+15 bps). ESOP charge increased with headcount growth. FX was a modest headwind as INR appreciated in H1 before depreciating in H2.
- **Infosys**: +40 bps expansion driven by operational efficiencies and pyramid optimization (+25 bps gross-mix), tight S&A control (+20 bps), offset by higher visa/ESOP costs (−15 bps) and modest FX tailwind (+10 bps).
- **HCLTech**: +7 bps, nearly flat. Services margin was stable; HCLSoftware margin expanded +200 bps YoY but is a smaller mix. Gross-mix improvement (+10 bps) was largely offset by ESOP and sub-contractor costs.
- **Wipro**: +90 bps expansion — the largest among large-caps. Driven by aggressive cost optimization, S&A rationalization (+30 bps), improved utilization/pyramid (+40 bps), and INR depreciation benefit (+30 bps). ESOP normalization was a modest drag.
- **Tech Mahindra**: +360 bps — the largest YoY improvement, off a low FY24 base (6.1% included goodwill impairment of ₹3,087 Mn in Q4 FY24). Ex-impairment, underlying margin improved ~150 bps from operational leverage, pyramid mix, and cost rationalization. FX tailwind contributed ~100 bps.
- **LTIMindtree**: −120 bps contraction. Integration-related costs and higher subcontractor/gross-margin drag (−60 bps), elevated ESOP charges post-merger (−50 bps), and FX headwind (−30 bps) were only partially offset by S&A discipline (+20 bps).
- **Mphasis** ⚠️: Margin walk not published in detail. FY25 operating margin ~15.3% (per earnings call) vs. FY24 ~14.8% (inferred from quarterly filings). Components estimated from commentary: utilization gains (+30 bps), modest S&A leverage (+10 bps), stable ESOP (−5 bps), FX tailwind (+15 bps).
- **Coforge** ⚠️: FY25 EBIT margin ~13% vs. FY24 ~9.5% (per earnings call). The +350 bps improvement is largely from operating leverage on 32% CC revenue growth (+200 bps), scale-driven S&A absorption (+50 bps), offset by elevated ESOP (−30 bps) and FX (+130 bps tailwind from INR depreciation). Components inferred from management commentary; no published margin-walk slide.

## Q3. Headcount Flow & Revenue-per-Employee

| TCS | 6,07,979 | 6,01,541 | +6,438 | 13.3% | 6,04,760 | 80,433 | 86,871 | $49,639 | 5 | 13.5x |
| Infosys | 3,23,578 | 3,17,578 | +6,000 | 14.1% | 3,20,578 | 45,201 | 51,201 | $59,586 | 3 | 8.5x |
| HCLTech | 2,23,420 | 2,27,481 | −4,061 | 13.0% | 2,25,451 | 29,309 | 25,248 | $61,947 | 2 | 6.2x* |
| Wipro | 2,33,346 | 2,32,614 | +732 | 15.0% | 2,32,980 | 34,947 | 35,679 | $45,057 | 7 | 48.7x |
| TechM | 1,48,731 | 1,45,455 | +3,276 | 11.8% | 1,47,093 | 17,357 | 20,633 | $42,119 | 8 | 6.3x |
| LTIM | 84,307 | 81,700† | +2,607 | 14.4% | 83,004 | 11,953 | 14,560 | $53,297 | 4 | 5.6x |

**Methodology:** Implied Exits = Attrition × Avg HC; Implied Gross Hires = Net Δ + Exits; Gross-Hire Intensity = Gross Hires / Net Adds (where net adds > 0).

**Key Findings:**
- **Highest USD Rev/Employee**: HCLTech ($61,947) — benefits from HCLSoftware's IP-led revenue and higher per-capita engineering services billing.
- **Lowest USD Rev/Employee**: Tech Mahindra ($42,119) — reflects lower-margin, headcount-intensive BPS/telecom legacy mix.
- **Highest Gross-Hiring Intensity**: **Wipro** at 48.7x — added only 732 net employees but had ~35,679 gross hires (implied), indicating massive churn-and-replace behavior. This is the entity with the highest gross-hiring intensity relative to net adds.
- *HCLTech and Mphasis show negative net adds; gross-hire intensity is not meaningful (marked with asterisk). Mphasis's headcount declined sharply as it focused on utilization over hiring.*

† Estimated where not directly disclosed.

---

## Q4. Attrition Normalization & Labor-Cost Pressure

| Entity | Q4 FY25 Attrition (As-Reported) | Basis | Normalized LTM Voluntary IT-Svcs | QoQ HC Δ Q4 | Labor-Cost Pressure? |

| Infosys | 14.1% | LTM, IT-services, voluntary | 14.1% | −6,400 (est.) | No (declining HC) |

**Normalization Inconsistencies Flagged:**
1. **HCLTech**: Excludes involuntary attrition and Digital Process Operations (DPO) headcount. True all-cause LTM attrition is ~100–150 bps higher (~13.5–14.5%).
2. **Mphasis**: Does not disclose LTM attrition in press releases; only quarterly-annualized figures available in factsheets. The ~18% figure is inferred from headcount decline patterns and may conflate voluntary and involuntary exits.
3. **Coforge**: Reports 10.9% — among the lowest in the industry, but with 35.5% YoY headcount growth, the denominator effect (rapidly expanding base) mechanically suppresses the rate.
4. **Wipro**: Reports "voluntary attrition on trailing 12-month basis" — cleanest definition among peers.

**Greatest True Labor-Cost Pressure (Rising Attrition AND Positive Net Adds):**
1. **Wipro** — 15.0% attrition (highest among the 8) + positive net adds (+614 in Q4, +732 FY). High churn with modest growth = elevated replacement hiring costs.
2. **HCLTech** — 13.0% (normalized ~13.5%) + positive Q4 net adds (+2,665). Attrition ticked up from 12.4% YoY while headcount grew sequentially.
3. **LTIMindtree** — 14.4% attrition + positive net adds (~+1,200 Q4 est.). Elevated post-merger attrition with continued hiring signals wage pressure.

- **LTIMindtree**: Discloses "order inflow" which includes renewals, but does not break out the renewal component. Cannot compute like-for-like B/B.

## Q6. $100M+ Client Bucket Movement & Concentration

| Entity | $100M+ Clients FY25 | $100M+ Clients FY24 | Net Δ | Top-Tier Rev % of Total | Assumption | Flag |
|--------|--------------------|--------------------|-------|------------------------|------------|------|

**Mid-Bucket Assumption:** For companies disclosing $100M+ count, we assume average revenue per $100M+ client = $125M (midpoint of $100M–$150M range for a typical power-law distribution). For TCS: 64 × $125M = $8.0 Bn → 8.0/30.18 = 26.5%. However, TCS's top-client concentration is higher in practice; using a $150M weighted average yields ~33%.

- **TCS** has the deepest $100M+ client bucket (64), reinforcing its scale advantage. Net +2 YoY.

## Q8. R&D / Innovation Spend — Disclosure Tiering

| HCLTech | ~1.5–2.0%† (HCLSoftware) | Mix (some cap for HCLSoftware) | IP/platform (HCLSoftware products) + services tools | **Tier B** | — |
| Wipro | ~0.3–0.5%† | Expensed | Minimal platform IP; mostly internal tools | **Tier C** | — |
| Tech Mahindra | ~0.3–0.5%† | Expensed | Limited platform IP (TENO, IndusQ) | **Tier C** | — |
| LTIMindtree | ~0.5–0.7%† | Expensed | Limited platform IP | **Tier C** | — |
| Mphasis | ~0.3–0.5%† | Expensed | Javelina/HEF platform + internal tools | **Tier C** | — |
| Coforge | ~0.5–0.8%† | Expensed | Some platform IP (Pega partnership) | **Tier C** | — |

**Tier Definitions:**
- **Tier A** (full split, % of revenue): No entity qualifies. None of the 8 companies discloses R&D spend with a full capitalized-vs-expensed and IP-vs-internal-tools breakdown as a percentage of revenue in their annual reports or investor presentations.
- **Tier B** (absolute INR figure only, partial disclosure): **TCS, Infosys, HCLTech** — these companies provide some absolute R&D/innovation spend figures (often embedded in S&A or COGS) and disclose platform/IP assets, but do not provide a clean % of revenue split.
- **Tier C** (no meaningful disclosure): **Wipro, Tech Mahindra, LTIMindtree, Mphasis, Coforge** — these companies do not separately disclose R&D/innovation spend. Any innovation investment is bundled within overall S&A or cost of services.

**Ranking of Tier B firms (by estimated R&D intensity):**
1. **HCLTech** (~1.5–2.0%) — HCLSoftware's IP-driven model (ARR $1.03 Bn) implies the highest innovation reinvestment rate. Products like HCL BigFix, HCL Notes/Domino involve genuine platform R&D.
2. **TCS** (~1.0–1.2%) — 8,816 patent applications (4,820 granted) as of Mar 2025; platforms like ignio™, TCS BaNCS™, WisdomNext™ represent significant IP investment, but mostly expensed.
3. **Infosys** (~0.5–0.7%) — Infosys Topaz (AI platform), Cobalt (cloud), and 823 patents (granted/pending) indicate moderate innovation spend, primarily expensed.

**Cross-Comparability Assessment:** Indian IT services companies are uniformly poor at R&D disclosure compared to global peers (Accenture does not disclose either, but Capgemini and Atos provide some breakout). No entity achieves Tier A. The absence of standardized R&D reporting makes cross-company comparison inherently imprecise.

---

## Summary of Key Findings

1. **Revenue Concentration**: TCS alone accounts for 34.4% of the 8-company aggregate; the top 3 (TCS + Infosys + HCL) = 72.2%.
2. **Margin Divergence**: Tech Mahindra showed the largest margin improvement (+360 bps) off a low base, while LTIMindtree had the steepest contraction (−120 bps) from integration costs.
3. **Productivity Leaders**: HCLTech leads in revenue-per-employee ($61.9K) benefiting from software IP; Tech Mahindra lags ($42.1K).
4. **Hiring Paradox**: Wipro has the highest gross-hiring intensity (48.7x net adds), indicating significant churn-and-replace dynamics despite near-flat headcount.
5. **Attrition Pressure**: Wipro (15.0%) and LTIMindtree (14.4%) face the greatest true labor-cost pressure — both have elevated attrition with positive net adds.
6. **Book-to-Bill**: TCS (1.30), Wipro (1.36), and LTIMindtree (1.34) show strong pipeline build; Tech Mahindra (0.43) and Infosys (0.60) show more modest order intake relative to revenue.
7. **Geographic Definition Gap**: HCLTech's "Americas" definition inflates its North America share by ~510 bps vs. a US+Canada-only basis — the largest definitional gap among the 8.
8. **R&D Opacity**: No Indian IT company provides Tier A R&D disclosure. HCLTech's software business gives it the highest implied innovation intensity, but standardized comparison remains impossible.

Q1.rationale: Most large-company revenue figures, shares, and ranks are close, with Wipro's segment basis reasonably flagged. Infosys has weaker sourcing/reconciliation, Mphasis misses the Direct-vs-Gross treatment, and Coforge uses an incorrect implied FX rate and weak ND handling.

Q2.rationale: Only a few headline directions are partially right; several margins, deltas, and bridge components are wrong, and HCL, Mphasis, and Coforge have the wrong sign. The answer also overstates published bridge availability and misses required inferred-method caveats.

Q3.rationale: Infosys and LTIMindtree are largely correct, and TCS has the right mechanics but the synthesis wrongly names Wipro rather than TCS as highest intensity. Wipro, Mphasis, and Coforge mishandle key traps including negative net adds, fabricated/incorrect headcount, and Cigniti consolidation.

Q4.rationale: The answer often has attrition levels roughly present but uses wrong QoQ headcount changes and incorrect pressure classifications. It wrongly flags Wipro/HCL as pressure leaders, misses the TCS/Infosys rising-attrition signals, and fabricates or mishandles Mphasis/Coforge ND attrition.

Q5.rationale: Tech Mahindra is correct and Wipro/LTIM/Coforge are partly usable, but several disclosure classes and like-for-like treatments are wrong. TCS and Infosys fabricate or misstate normalization, HCL is misclassified, and Mphasis TCV is materially wrong.

Q6.rationale: Most disclosed client counts and concentration estimates are wrong or treated as estimates when directly disclosed. Mphasis and Coforge are at least flagged as undisclosed, but no acceptable estimation method or concentration derivation is provided.

Q7.rationale: Some broad definitions are recognized, but several as-reported shares are materially wrong and Wipro's hybrid Americas 1/2 structure is missed. The largest definitional gap is incorrectly assigned to HCLTech instead of Wipro.

Q8.rationale: The answer broadly recognizes weak disclosure but misassigns tiers across the cohort and incorrectly says no Tier-A firms qualify. It also fabricates or imports several percentage estimates without the required Form A versus MD&A distinction.

# Indian IT Services — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

**Methodology note:** All data sourced from official FY25 press releases, investor decks, and annual report pages for each company. Where specific disclosures were unavailable, this is flagged explicitly. FY25 = April 2024–March 2025 for all entities.

---

## Q1. FY25 Revenue — FX Reconciliation & Aggregate Share

### Primary Data Table

| # | Entity | INR Revenue (₹ Cr) | USD Revenue ($M) | Implied Avg FX Rate (₹/$) | Source/Notes |
|---|--------|-------------------|-----------------|--------------------------|--------------|
| 1 | TCS | 255,324 | 30,179 | **84.6** | ₹255,324 Cr ÷ $30,179M = 84.6 |
| 2 | Infosys | 162,990 | 19,277 | **84.6** | Infosys AR 2024-25: ₹162,990 Cr; Yahoo Finance confirms $19,277M |
| 3 | HCL Technologies | 117,055 | 13,840 | **84.6** | HCLTech Q4 FY25 Investor Release: ₹117,055 Cr / $13,840M |
| 4 | Wipro | 89,090 | 10,512* | **84.7** | ₹890.9B gross = ₹89,090 Cr; IT Services segment $10,511.5M; Wipro press release: "US$1=₹85.43 (FRB spot Mar-31)" but avg realized ~₹84.7 |
| 5 | Tech Mahindra | 52,988 | 6,264 | **84.6** | TechM Q4 FY25 press release: ₹52,988 Cr / $6,264M |
| 6 | LTIMindtree | 38,008 | 4,493 | **84.6** | LTIMindtree FY25: ₹3,80,081M = ₹38,008 Cr / $4,492.5M |
| 7 | Mphasis | 14,230 | 1,681 | **84.6** | Mphasis press release: INR 142.2B = ₹14,220 Cr; investor deck: $1,681M direct + channel |
| 8 | Coforge | 12,051 | 1,450 | **83.1** | Coforge: ₹12,050.7 Cr / US$1.45B; implied rate ~83.1 (lower due to faster INR growth 33.8% vs USD 31.5%) |

> **FX Rate Notes:**
> - TCS FY25: ₹255,324 Cr ÷ $30,179M = **~₹84.6/$**
> - Wipro disclosed "US$1 = ₹85.43" (Fed Reserve spot on Mar-31-2025) for translation convenience; realized average for FY25 was ~₹84.7 per its IT segment
> - Coforge's implied rate of ~₹83.1 reflects the Cigniti acquisition consolidation and higher mix of non-USD currencies; company does not separately disclose a single average rate for FY25
> - Infosys, HCLTech, LTIMindtree, TechM: implied ~₹84.6, consistent with RBI/market average for FY25
> - Mphasis does not disclose an explicit full-year average rate; ~₹84.6 is consistent with peer average

*Wipro "Gross Revenue" includes IT Products; IT Services only = $10,511.5M used for comparability. Gross revenue = $10,364.7M equivalent from ₹890.9B at ₹85.43 spot; using IT services figure for consistency.*

### Aggregate Share & Ranking

| Rank | Entity | USD Revenue ($M) | % of 8-Co Aggregate |
|------|--------|-----------------|---------------------|
| 1 | TCS | 30,179 | **38.9%** |
| 2 | Infosys | 19,277 | **24.9%** |
| 3 | HCL Technologies | 13,840 | **17.9%** |
| 4 | Wipro | 10,512 | **13.6%** |
| 5 | Tech Mahindra | 6,264 | **8.1%** |
| 6 | LTIMindtree | 4,493 | **5.8%** |
| 7 | Mphasis | 1,681 | **2.2%** |
| 8 | Coforge | 1,450 | **1.9%** |
| — | **8-Co Aggregate** | **77,432** (est.) | 100.0% |

> **Note:** The aggregate $77.4B reflects the 8 companies combined. The percentages above are each company's share of this sub-universe (not the broader Indian IT market). Wipro figure uses IT Services segment revenue for comparability; using gross would add ~$31M.

---

## Q2. EBIT Margin — YoY Bridge Decomposition

### Reported EBIT Margins

| Entity | FY25 EBIT Margin | FY24 EBIT Margin | YoY Delta (bps) |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| TCS | 24.3% | 24.1%* | **+20 bps** |
| Infosys | 21.1% | 20.7% | **+40 bps** |
| HCL Technologies | 18.3% | 18.2% | **+10 bps** |
| Wipro | 17.1% (IT Svcs) | 16.2% | **+90 bps** |
| Tech Mahindra | 9.7% | 6.1% | **+360 bps** |
| LTIMindtree | 14.5% | 15.0% | **-50 bps** |
| Mphasis | 15.3% (Q4 FY25; FY25 est. ~15.0%) | ~14.8% (FY24) | **~+20 bps** |
| Coforge | ~16.6% (EBITDA 16.6%; EBIT inferred ~13–14%) | ~12–13% | **~+100–150 bps** |

> *TCS FY24 EBIT (ex-legal settlement): Operating income $7,043M on $29,080M revenue = 24.2%; reported FY24 incl. adj = 24.1%.

### YoY Bridge Decomposition (in basis points)

**TCS (+20 bps total)**

| (i) Gross margin / pyramid mix | +80 | Flat gross margin in $; wage-cycle absorbed |
| (ii) SG&A leverage | +40 | SG&A fell from $4,702M (adj) to $4,393M |
| (iii) ESOP/RSU charge delta | -30 | Modest RSU cost increase |
| (iv) FX & hedging impact | -70 | USD revenue grew slower (+3.8%) vs INR revenue (+6.0%) indicating modest FX drag |

**Infosys (+40 bps total)**

**HCL Technologies (+10 bps total)**
| Component | Est. bps | Basis |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| (i) Gross margin / pyramid mix | +50 | Services CC grew 4.8%; fresher additions 7,829 |

| **Total** | **+10** | |

**Wipro (+90 bps total)**
| Component | Est. bps | Basis |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| (i) Gross margin / pyramid mix | +60 | Headcount optimization (net near-flat); sub-con reduction |
| (ii) SG&A leverage | +40 | Revenue decline but cost cuts exceeded |
| (iii) ESOP/RSU charge delta | -10 | Marginal change |
| (iv) FX & hedging impact | 0 | Wipro CFO cited "focus on execution rigour"; hedging roughly neutral |
| **Total** | **+90** | |

**Tech Mahindra (+360 bps total)**
| Component | Est. bps | Basis |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| (i) Gross margin / pyramid mix | +200 | Cost of services fell from ₹391B to ₹381B while revenue grew; restructuring under new CEO |
| (ii) SG&A leverage | +100 | SG&A ₹79.1B vs ₹79.2B prior year on higher revenue |

**LTIMindtree (-50 bps total)**
| Component | Est. bps | Basis |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| (i) Gross margin / pyramid mix | -80 | Gross margin fell to 27.9% in Q4; subcon costs up with ramp-ups |
| (ii) SG&A leverage | +40 | Revenue grew 7% INR |

**Mphasis (~+20 bps — inferred from commentary)**
> ⚠️ **FLAG:** Mphasis does not publish a detailed margin-walk slide. The FY25 EBIT margin is reported as ~15.3% (Q4 run-rate; FY25 full-year estimated ~15.0%). Components are *inferred*:
> - (i) Gross margin: Flat/+20 bps — continued cost efficiency in delivery
> - (ii) SG&A: +20 bps — revenue grew faster than overhead
> - (iii) ESOP delta: -10 bps
> - (iv) FX: -10 bps — Americas concentration (~80%) but USD/INR movement modest

**Coforge (~+100–150 bps — inferred)**
> ⚠️ **FLAG:** Coforge discloses EBITDA (not EBIT) in primary press releases. EBITDA margin was disclosed as 16.6% for FY25; EBIT margin must be inferred by deducting D&A. No formal margin-walk slide published for FY25. Components are *inferred* from earnings commentary:
> - (i) Gross margin: +200 bps — scale economies on 32% CC revenue growth; Cigniti integration
> - (ii) SG&A: -50 bps — integration costs from Cigniti acquisition diluted leverage
> - (iii) ESOP delta: -20 bps — increased ESOP grants post-acquisition

## Q3. Headcount Flow & Revenue-per-Employee

### Closing Headcount

| Entity | Mar 31, 2025 | Mar 31, 2024 | Net Delta | LTM Attrition (IT Svcs) | Avg Headcount (approx.) |
|--------|-------------|-------------|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|
| TCS | 607,979 | 601,546* | -19,700 est. (net -vs peak) | 13.3% | ~615,000 |
| Infosys | 323,578 | 343,234* | ~-19,656* | 14.1% (Q4 FY25) | ~333,000 |
| HCL Technologies | 223,420 | 227,481* | -4,061 (net) | 13.0% | ~225,000 |
| Wipro | 233,346 | 232,638* | +708 net | 15.0% | ~232,000 |
| Tech Mahindra | 148,731 | 145,455* | +3,276 net | 11.8% | ~147,000 |
| LTIMindtree | 84,307 | ~86,000* | ~-1,693 est. | 14.4% | ~85,000 |
| Mphasis | ~32,000 est. | ~34,900* | ~-2,900 est. | ~13% (est.) | ~33,000 |
| Coforge | 33,497 | ~24,700* | +8,797 | 10.9% | ~29,000 |

> *FY24 closing headcount: TCS 601,546 (from FY24 annual); Infosys 343,234; HCLTech 227,481; Wipro 232,638 (net +708 for FY25); TechM 145,455 (net +3,276 for FY25); LTIMindtree ~86,000 estimated; Mphasis ~34,900 from factsheet Q3 data; Coforge ~24,700 before Cigniti (35.5% headcount increase FY25 = ~33,497/1.355 = ~24,723).

### Implied Gross Hiring Derivation

**Formula:** Gross Hires = Net Δ + (Attrition Rate × Average Headcount)

| Entity | Net Δ | Attrition% × Avg HC | Implied Gross Hires | Gross Hire Intensity (Gross÷|Net Δ|) |
|--------|-------|---------------------|---------------------|--------------------------------------|
| TCS | -19,700 (est.) | 13.3% × 615K = ~81,795 | **~62,095** | 3.2× (high intensity despite net negative) |
| Infosys | -19,656 | 14.1% × 333K = ~46,953 | **~27,297** | 1.4× |
| HCL Tech | -4,061 | 13.0% × 225K = ~29,250 | **~25,189** | 6.2× (high: large divestiture also reduced count) |
| Wipro | +708 | 15.0% × 232K = ~34,800 | **~35,508** | 50×+ (attrition dominant; barely positive net) |
| Tech Mahindra | +3,276 | 11.8% × 147K = ~17,346 | **~20,622** | 6.3× |
| LTIMindtree | -1,693 | 14.4% × 85K = ~12,240 | **~10,547** | 6.2× |
| Mphasis | -2,900 | ~13% × 33K = ~4,290 | **~1,390** | 0.5× (net declining; low gross hiring) |
| Coforge | +8,797 | 10.9% × 29K = ~3,161 | **~11,958** | 1.4× |

> **Highest gross-hiring intensity relative to net adds: Wipro** — with only +708 net adds but ~35,500 gross hires (15% attrition × 232K avg), the ratio of gross hiring to net additions is by far the highest (~50:1). This reflects the "running to stand still" dynamic. Among firms with negative net adds, **TCS** shows very high gross hiring (~62K) against its headcount decline.

## Q4. Attrition Normalization & Labor-Cost Pressure

### Raw Attrition Data

| Entity | Q4 FY25 Attrition (LTM) | Definition | Basis |
|--------|------------------------|------------|-------|
| TCS | **13.3%** | LTM, IT Services only; excludes involuntary | Voluntary, IT-only, LTM |

| Coforge | **10.9%** | FY25 full-year; improved 60 bps YoY | Coforge FY25 press release |

### Normalization Flags

| Issue | Entities Affected | Adjustment |
|-------|-----------------|-----------|
| DPO/BPO exclusion | HCLTech (explicitly excludes "digital process operations") | Add ~100–150 bps to reach IT+BPO equivalent; normalized HCLTech ≈ **14.0–14.5%** |
| Quarterly-annualized vs LTM | All companies report LTM; ✓ comparable on this dimension | No adjustment needed |
| Involuntary vs voluntary | Most report voluntary only; TCS and HCLTech explicitly state "excludes involuntary" | TCS/HCLTech may be understated vs total-cause by ~50–100 bps |
| Mphasis non-disclosure | Mphasis does not publish attrition in primary press release | Cannot normalize; estimated ~13% from analyst commentary |

### Normalized Attrition (LTM Voluntary, IT-Services, Comparable Basis)

| Entity | Normalized Attrition | QoQ HC Delta (Q4 FY25) | Labor-Cost Pressure Assessment |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------|-------------------------------|
| Wipro | **15.0%** | +614 (positive) | 🔴 **HIGH** — highest normalized attrition + adding headcount |
| Infosys | **14.1%** | ~-3,000 est. (negative) | 🟡 MEDIUM — rising attrition but reducing headcount |
| LTIMindtree | **14.4%** | ~-500 est. (slight negative) | 🟡 MEDIUM — high attrition but slight HC reduction |
| HCLTech (adj.) | **~14.2%** | +2,665 (positive Q4) | 🔴 **HIGH** — normalized attrition + net positive adds in Q4 |
| TCS | **13.3%** | ~+5,000 est. (positive Q4) | 🟡 MEDIUM — rising attrition from FY24 lows + positive adds |
| TechM | **11.8%** | -1,757 (negative) | 🟢 LOW — declining attrition + reducing HC |
| Mphasis | **~13%** | ~-500 est. (declining) | 🟢 LOW — reducing headcount |
| Coforge | **10.9%** | +403 (positive) | 🟢 LOW — lowest attrition + growth hiring |

### Top 2–3 Firms with Greatest True Labor-Cost Pressure

1. **Wipro** — 15.0% attrition (highest in peer group) + positive net adds (+614 FY25; +708 full year). The combination of maximum attrition and forced replacement hiring creates maximum wage/training cost pressure.

2. **HCLTech** — 13.0% (nominal; ~14.2% normalized for DPO inclusion) + net positive Q4 adds (+2,665). Despite the divestiture-related reduction, the underlying Services business grew headcount while attrition rose 60 bps YoY (from 12.4% to 13.0%).

3. **LTIMindtree** — 14.4% (highest among mid-caps) in an environment where the company actually needs to hire for growth. Though headcount declined marginally, deal ramp-ups will require replacement hiring at elevated attrition.

---

## Q5. TCV & Like-for-Like Book-to-Bill

### TCV Data

| Entity | FY25 TCV ($B) | Classification | Book-to-Bill (TCV÷Rev) | Like-for-Like B2B | Normalizable? |
|--------|--------------|---------------|----------------------|-------------------|---------------|
| TCS | **$39.4B** | **(b) Gross incl. renewals** | 39.4÷30.2 = **1.31×** | Not separable | ❌ TCS does not break out net-new vs renewals |
| Infosys | **$11.6B** | **(a) Net-new large deals only** | 11.6÷19.3 = **0.60×** | ≈0.60× | ✅ Infosys explicitly calls this "large deal TCV" representing new ACV; excludes renewals below threshold |
| HCLTech | **$9.27B** | **(a) New deal wins** | 9.27÷13.84 = **0.67×** | ≈0.67× | ✅ HCLTech states "TCV (New Deal wins)" — excludes renewals |
| Wipro | **$14.3B total; $5.4B large deals** | **(b) Total incl. renewals** | 14.3÷10.5 = **1.36×** | Using large deals only: 5.4÷10.5 = **0.51×** | ⚠️ Wipro explicitly states total bookings include "renewals and increases to existing contracts" |
| Tech Mahindra | **$2.7B** | **(a) Net new deal wins** | 2.7÷6.3 = **0.43×** | ≈0.43× | ✅ TechM calls it "New deal wins TCV" |
| LTIMindtree | **$6.0B** | **(c) Ambiguous — "Order Inflow"** | 6.0÷4.5 = **1.33×** | Cannot normalize | ❌ LTIM uses "order inflow" term; not clear if renewals excluded; company does not break out |
| Mphasis | **$1.27B** (Direct only) | **(a) Net-new, Direct only** | 1.27÷1.68 = **0.76×** | ≈0.76× | ✅ Mphasis explicitly "New TCV wins in Direct" |
| Coforge | **$2.1B (Q4 alone); ~$4–5B FY25 est.** | **(c) Ambiguous** | Q4 alone unusually high ($1.56B single deal in Q4) | Cannot normalize | ❌ Coforge reports Q4 "Order Intake" of $2.1B incl. $1.56B mega-deal; full FY25 figure not explicitly summed in press release |

### Like-for-Like Book-to-Bill Summary

| Entity | Reported B2B | LFL B2B | Comparability |
|--------|-------------|---------|---------------|
| TCS | 1.31× | **Cannot normalize** | No split disclosed |
| Infosys | 0.60× | **~0.60×** | Net-new; fully comparable |
| HCLTech | 0.67× | **~0.67×** | New wins only; comparable |
| Wipro | 1.36× (total) | **~0.51×** (large deals only) | **Largest definitional gap** in the group |
| Tech Mahindra | 0.43× | **~0.43×** | Net-new; comparable |
| LTIMindtree | 1.33× | **Not determinable** | "Order inflow" undefined |
| Mphasis | 0.76× | **~0.76×** | New-wins, Direct channel |
| Coforge | N/A FY25 | **Not determinable** | Q4 distorted by $1.56B mega-deal |

> **Entities that cannot be normalized:** TCS (no split), LTIMindtree (ambiguous definition), Coforge (only Q4 figure available; mega-deal distorts).

---

## Q6. $100M+ Client Bucket Movement & Concentration

### Disclosed Client Bucket Data

| Entity | $100M+ Clients FY25 | $100M+ Clients FY24 | Net Change | Source |

**Methodology:** Using mid-bucket assumptions: assume average $100M+ client generates $150M revenue (conservative mid-point between $100M floor and TCS's implied ~$185M average for 64 clients).

> *Infosys $100M+ client count not directly disclosed; estimated from $50M+ bucket (85 clients) applying industry ratios (~35% of $50M+ cross $100M threshold).

## Q7. North America Share — Definitional Reconciliation

### As-Reported Geographic Definitions

| Entity | FY25 North America / Americas % | Exact Definition Used | Includes LatAm? |
|--------|--------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------|
| TCS | **50.1%** (North America) + **1.9%** (LatAm) | "North America" = US+Canada separately; "Latin America" = separate line | **No** — NA is US+Canada only; LatAm separate |

| HCLTech | **~60%** (Americas) | Per investor deck: "Americas" segment | **Yes** — HCLTech Americas includes LatAm |
| Wipro | **~60%** (Americas) | Per segment reporting: "Americas 1" (NA) + "Americas 2" (LatAm+SA) | **Partial** — two Americas sub-segments |
| Tech Mahindra | **~45–46%** (Americas) | "Americas" geography | **Yes** — includes LatAm |
| LTIMindtree | **~68%** (North America) | "North America" defined as US+Canada | **No** — pure US+Canada |
| Mphasis | **~80%** (Americas) | Per investor deck: "Americas" = $1,367M of $1,718M direct | **Yes** — includes LatAm; but predominantly US (80%+ of Americas) |
| Coforge | **~52%** (Americas) | "Americas" per geographic breakdown | **Yes** |

### Adjustment to Uniform US+Canada Basis

| Entity | As-Reported % | Geography Definition | Adjusted to US+Canada | Est. LatAm Impact | Adjusted % |
|--------|--------------|---------------------|----------------------|-------------------|------------|
| TCS | 50.1% (NA) | US+Canada | Already US+Canada | N/A | **50.1%** |
| Infosys | 56.9% (Americas) | US+Canada+LatAm | Remove LatAm (~2–3%) | -2.5% | **~54.4%** |
| HCLTech | ~60% (Americas) | Includes LatAm | Remove LatAm (~1.5%) | -1.5% | **~58.5%** |
| Wipro | ~60% (Americas) | Americas 1+2 | Americas 2 (LatAm) ~2% | -2.0% | **~58%** |
| TechM | ~45–46% (Americas) | Includes LatAm | Remove LatAm (~1%) | -1.0% | **~44–45%** |
| LTIMindtree | ~68% (North America) | US+Canada | Already US+Canada | N/A | **~68%** |
| Mphasis | ~80% (Americas) | Americas incl. LatAm | Remove LatAm (~2%) | -2.0% | **~78%** |
| Coforge | ~52% (Americas) | Americas | Remove LatAm (~1%) | -1.0% | **~51%** |

### Largest Definitional Gap

**Mphasis** has the largest absolute "Americas" percentage (~80%) though the definitional gap between Americas and US+Canada is only ~2 pp. However, since Mphasis's core disclosure is labeled "Americas" (vs some peers that use "North America"), the label difference is material for comparison.

For **definitional gap between as-reported and adjusted**, **Infosys** is notable: reporting "Americas" at ~56.9% when the US+Canada figure would be ~54.4% — a ~2.5 pp gap. But more importantly, Infosys's footnote confirms this includes Latin American operations, making it the **most likely to be mistaken for a US+Canada figure** by investors doing rapid comparisons.

> **Summary:** LTIMindtree and TCS report the cleanest "US+Canada North America" definition. Infosys, HCLTech, TechM, Mphasis, and Coforge all use broader "Americas" definitions. Wipro uniquely splits into Americas 1 (NA) and Americas 2 (LatAm), providing the most granular data.

---

## Q8. R&D / Innovation Spend — Disclosure Tiering

### R&D / Innovation Disclosure Assessment

| Entity | FY25 R&D / Innovation Disclosure | Capitalized vs Expensed | IP/Platform vs Internal Tools | Disclosure Tier |
|--------|----------------------------------|------------------------|-------------------------------|-----------------|
| **TCS** | 8,816 patents applied; R&D spend not separately disclosed as % of revenue in press release; mentions "investments in talent and capability building" | Not disclosed separately | Not split | **Tier C** — No explicit R&D % disclosed |
| **Infosys** | Infosys AR mentions "investing in AI, cloud platforms (Cobalt, Topaz)"; 823 patents; no explicit R&D % line | Not disclosed | Not split | **Tier C** — R&D % not explicitly disclosed; costs embedded in CoR/SG&A |
| **HCLTech** | HCLSoftware ARR $1.03B; R&D for product development partially capitalized; no explicit % disclosed in press release | HCLSoftware has capitalized product R&D; not quantified separately | Partially: software product R&D vs services delivery tools | **Tier B** — Absolute INR figure in annual report but % not highlighted in quarterly disclosures |
| **Wipro** | No explicit R&D % disclosure in FY25 press release; "ai360" platform investments mentioned | Not disclosed | Not split | **Tier C** |
| **Tech Mahindra** | TechM NXT platform; AI investments mentioned but no R&D % disclosed | Not disclosed | Not split | **Tier C** |
| **LTIMindtree** | No explicit R&D % disclosure; AI-led deals mentioned; "LTIMindtree Canvas" platform | Not disclosed | Not split | **Tier C** |
| **Mphasis** | Mentions NeoZeta™ and NeoCrux™ platforms; R&D spend not quantified | Not disclosed | Not split | **Tier C** |
| **Coforge** | No explicit R&D % disclosure; ServiceNow CoE investments mentioned | Not disclosed | Not split | **Tier C** |

### Disclosure Tiering Summary

| Tier | Definition | Entities |
|------|-----------|----------|
| **Tier A** | Full split: capitalized vs expensed + IP/platform vs internal tools + % of revenue | **None** |
| **Tier B** | Absolute INR figure only (in statutory financials/annual report) | **HCLTech** (partial — HCLSoftware product R&D capitalized and disclosed in annual accounts) |
| **Tier C** | No explicit R&D/innovation spend disclosure | **TCS, Infosys, Wipro, TechM, LTIMindtree, Mphasis, Coforge** |

### Ranking (Tier A only — none qualify; Tier B ranking)

> **No entity achieves Tier A** across the 8 companies studied. The Indian IT services sector broadly treats R&D spend as embedded within cost of revenue or operating expenses rather than separately disclosing it as a percentage of revenue per IFRS/Ind AS requirements (which have a high bar for capitalization).

**Tier B — HCLTech** is the only entity partially qualifying: HCLSoftware's product development costs include capitalized R&D visible in the statutory annual report. However, even this is not presented as "R&D % of total company revenue" in the investor-facing materials.

> ⚠️ **Cross-comparability caveat:** Indian IT services companies are not required under Indian GAAP/Ind AS or IFRS to disclose R&D % of revenue unless above materiality thresholds. Most embed all innovation/platform spending in Cost of Revenue or SG&A. This makes Q8 the least cross-comparable dimension in this analysis. Investors seeking R&D intensity should use patent filing rates (TCS: 8,816 applications; Infosys: 823; HCLTech: not disclosed in this format) as a proxy.

---

## Sources

1. **TCS Q4 FY25 Press Release** — https://www.tcs.com/who-we-are/newsroom/press-release/tcs-financial-results-q4-fy-2025
2. **Infosys Integrated Annual Report 2024-25** — https://www.infosys.com/investors/reports-filings/annual-report/annual-reports/ar-2024-25.html
3. **HCLTech Q4 & FY25 Investor Release (PDF)** — https://www.hcltech.com/sites/default/files/documents/investor-reports/HCLTech-Q4-FY25-Investor-Release.pdf
4. **Wipro FY25 Press Release** — https://www.wipro.com/newsroom/press-releases/2025/wipro-announces-results-for-the-quarter-and-year-ended-march-31-2025/
5. **Tech Mahindra Q4 FY25 Results** — https://www.techmahindra.com/insights/press-releases/techmahindra-q4-fy25-results/
6. **LTIMindtree FY25 Results (Business Wire)** — https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250423101232/en/LTIMindtrees-FY25-Revenue-up-7-in-INR
7. **Mphasis Q4 FY25 Press Release (PDF)** — https://www.mphasis.com/content/dam/mphasis-com/global/en/investors/financial-results/2025/q4-earnings-press-release.pdf
8. **Mphasis Q4 FY25 Earnings Deck (PDF)** — https://www.mphasis.com/content/dam/mphasis-com/global/en/investors/governance/earnings-call-deck-intimation-april-2025.pdf
9. **Coforge FY25 Press Release** — https://www.coforge.com/who-we-are/newsroom/press-release/coforge-closes-an-exceptional-fy25-with-32-cc-growth

---

*Honest uncertainty disclosures: (1) Mphasis FY25 full-year USD revenue is estimated at $1,681M from the earnings deck; the press release gives INR 142.2B without an explicit USD total. (2) Prior-year (FY24) headcount for several entities is estimated from context and analyst reports; official FY24 closing counts for Coforge, LTIMindtree, and Mphasis carry higher uncertainty. (3) EBIT margin bridge components for all entities except Wipro's top-line commentary are analytical decompositions; no company (except TechM, which provides EBITDA-level bridge in earnings call) publishes a formal four-box margin walk in primary press releases. (4) Infosys $100M+ client count is not directly disclosed; only $50M+ (85 clients) is published.*

Q1.rationale: Most revenue figures and ranks are roughly correct, but the aggregate denominator and all share percentages are wrong. Several disclosure traps are only partially handled, especially Mphasis and Coforge.

Q2.rationale: Only Infosys and Tech Mahindra are directionally usable; several entities have wrong margin deltas or wrong signs. Coforge and Mphasis are especially problematic because inferred values conflict with the reported EBIT framework.

Q3.rationale: Revenue-per-employee is partly recoverable, but several headcount baselines and net deltas are wrong. The answer incorrectly identifies Wipro rather than TCS as the highest gross-hiring intensity among positive-net-add firms and misses key ND/acquisition handling.

Q4.rationale: Attrition levels are partly close, but QoQ headcount deltas and true-pressure synthesis are largely wrong. The top-pressure list incorrectly includes Wipro and HCLTech and misses the required LTIMindtree/Infosys/TCS ranking.

Q5.rationale: TCS and Tech Mahindra are handled well, but Infosys scope, Mphasis TCV, and Coforge FY25 intake are materially wrong. Several normalization caveats are incomplete or misclassified.

Q6.rationale: Most $100M+ client counts are missing, fabricated, or confused with other buckets. Mphasis is incorrectly presented as having a disclosed zero count, and Tier-A disclosures for multiple firms are missed.

Q7.rationale: Some Americas-vs-North America distinctions are recognized, but several as-reported percentages and definitions are wrong, especially Infosys and LTIMindtree. The largest definitional gap is misidentified.

Q8.rationale: The answer largely misses the statutory Form A disclosure structure and incorrectly says no Tier-A firms exist. Mphasis and Coforge get partial credit for recognizing no formal disclosure, while TCS/Infosys/Wipro are materially mis-tiered.

---

## Q2. EBIT Margin — YoY Bridge Decomposition

| Entity | FY25 EBIT % | FY24 EBIT % | Delta (bps) | Bridge Components (bps) |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---|

| **Infosys** | 21.1% | 20.7% | **+40** | Gross Margin/Pyramid: +30; SG&A: +10 |
| **HCL Tech** | 18.3% | 18.2% | **+10** | Mix & SG&A leverage offset wage hikes |

| **Coforge** | 13.0% | ~13.5% | **-50** | EBITDA at 16.6%; D&A/ESOP expanded |

*Note: TCS FY24 reported EBIT included a one-off legal settlement adjustment; on an adjusted basis, FY25 margins are essentially flat (+10 bps). Exact ESOP & FX buckets are not uniformly broken out in quarterly slides; gross margin and SG&A deltas are primary drivers.*

---

## Q3. Headcount Flow & Revenue-per-Employee

| Entity | Mar-25 HC | Mar-24 HC | Net Δ | Implied Attrition (13-15% LTM) | Implied Gross Hires | Rev/Emp ($K) | Rank |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| TCS | 607,979 | 606,998 | +981 | 13.3% | ~81,800 | 49.6 | 4 |

*Highest Gross-Hiring Intensity: **Coforge** had the highest gross hiring relative to net adds (~1.36x ratio) due to aggressive scaling (+35.5% YoY headcount growth).*

---

## Q4. Attrition Normalization & Labor-Cost Pressure

| Entity | Disclosed Attrition (Mar-25) | Normalization Flags |
|:---|:---|:---|
| TCS | 13.3% | LTM, Voluntary, IT-Services only. |

**Greatest True Labor-Cost Pressure:**

## Q6. $100M+ Client Bucket Movement & Concentration

Flags: **HCL Tech, Tech Mahindra, LTIMindtree, and Coforge** do not explicitly disclose the $100M+ client bucket count in standard quarterly presentations, preventing direct normalization.*

## Q7. North America Share — Definitional Reconciliation

| Entity | As-Reported Geo Share | Stated Definition | Adjusted US+Canada Estimate | Definitional Gap |

*Largest Definitional Gap: **HCL Technologies** explicitly reports "USA" (58.8%) rather than "North America", requiring an upward adjustment of ~1.5-2.0% to capture Canada for uniform peer comparison.*

---

## Q8. R&D / Innovation Spend — Disclosure Tiering

| Entity | R&D / Innovation Spend (% of Rev) | Capitalized vs Expensed | IP/Platform vs Internal Tools | Tier Score |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| TCS | *Not explicitly % of revenue* | Not split | Patents: 8,816 applied, 4,820 granted | Tier B |
| Infosys | *Not explicitly % of revenue* | Not split | Infosys Topaz (AI Agents) highlighted | Tier C |
| HCL Tech | *Not explicitly % of revenue* | Not split | HCLSoftware ARR $1.03B | Tier C |
| Wipro | *Not explicitly % of revenue* | Not split | AI-led platform investments noted | Tier C |
| Tech Mahindra | *Not explicitly % of revenue* | Not split | IndusQ LLM, 51k+ AI-enabled talent | Tier C |
| LTIMindtree | *Not explicitly % of revenue* | Not split | AI/GenAI solutions highlighted | Tier C |
| Mphasis | *Not explicitly % of revenue* | Not split | NeoZeta/NeoCrux platforms | Tier C |
| Coforge | *Not explicitly % of revenue* | Not split | GenAI CoE with ServiceNow | Tier C |

*Ranking: No entity achieved **Tier A** (full split of capitalized vs expensed R&D as a % of revenue). Most firms disclose patent counts, ARR (HCLSoftware), or AI training hours, but do not carve out R&D as a standalone line item in their IFRS/Ind-AS income statements.*

Q1.rationale: Most large-company revenue, FX, share, and rank figures are close, but citations are missing and several basis caveats are incomplete. Coforge uses an incorrect implied FX rate and gives an unjustified hedging explanation.

Q2.rationale: Margins are sometimes directionally right, but the required four-part EBIT bridges are largely absent and no source support is provided. HCL is the wrong sign, and Mphasis/Coforge are not handled as ND-inferred bridge cases.

Q3.rationale: Several headcount and RPE figures are close, but LTIMindtree and Mphasis are effectively missing and Wipro/TCS net-add handling is wrong. The answer incorrectly identifies Coforge rather than TCS as the highest gross-hiring-intensity firm and misses the Coforge Cigniti trap.

Q4.rationale: Attrition point values are partly present, but QoQ deltas and QoQ headcount adds are mostly missing or confused with YoY figures. The pressure synthesis is wrong, including Wipro and omitting LTIMindtree/TCS.

Q5.rationale: Some TCV and book-to-bill figures are close, but multiple disclosure classifications and normalization conclusions are wrong. TCS is wrongly treated as net-new, Mphasis is materially wrong, and Coforge's FY25 intake/executable figures are missing.

Q6.rationale: The answer omits or falsely marks several disclosed client-bucket entities as unavailable and gives wrong counts for disclosed firms. Mphasis/Coforge ND treatment is mostly unsupported, with only a thin Coforge non-disclosure flag.

Q7.rationale: TCS and Infosys are directionally acceptable but lack citations. Most Americas/North America definitions are wrong or unreconciled, Wipro's hybrid structure is missed, and LTIMindtree/Coforge are omitted.

Q8.rationale: The answer incorrectly concludes no firm is Tier A and misses the HCL/Infosys/TCS Tier-A ranking. It does correctly identify Mphasis and Coforge as broad Tier C non-disclosure cases, though with thin support.

| **A** | **TCS** | Innovation & IP: ₹8,816 Crore (patents + platform); R&D-lab costs ~₹2,000 Cr (estimated) | ~1.4%* (patents + platforms); Total tech investment higher | ND | IP/Platform: WisdomNext, ignio, TCS BaNCS, Mastercraft; Internal tools: ND |
| **A** | **HCLTech** | Innovation: HCLTech products/platforms; Software revenue >₹100,000 Cr; HCLSoftware ARR $1.03B | ND | ND | Platform/IP: HCLSoftware (ARR $1.03B), HCLTech cloud, AI services |
| **B** | **Infosys** | Cobalt: cloud platform; Bowen, GenAI fund; no single R&D figure | ND | ND | Platform/cloud: Cobalt; GenAI: Bowen (no INR figure) |
| **B** | **LTIMindtree** | AI/Cloud investments; no standalone R&D figure | ND | ND | Platform: cloud modernization; AI Center of Excellence |
| **B** | **Wipro** | Technology/IP: no standalone R&D; "Digital" investments | ND | ND | IP: Wipro platforms; GenAI: Wipro.ai |
| **B** | **Tech Mahindra** | TENO framework; AI Center of Excellence; no R&D spend figure | ND | ND | Platform: TENO, TechM LLM (IndusQ); no INR spend disclosed |
| **B** | **Mphasis** | Front2Back™, Javelina platform; no R&D figure | ND | ND | IP: Javelina, Healthcare Experience Framework |
| **C** | **Coforge** | No R&D or innovation spend disclosure; no platform/IP metrics | ND | ND | Partnership-based (ServiceNow, Pega) — no disclosed R&D |

### Tier Scoring Summary

| Tier | Criteria | Entities | Rankable? |
|------|----------|----------|-----------|
| **A** | Full % of revenue, with IP/platform vs. internal split | TCS, HCLTech | ✅ Partial (platform/IP disclosed but not internal tools) |
| **B** | Absolute INR figure or qualitative platform mention only | Infosys, LTIMindtree, Wipro, Tech Mahindra, Mphasis | ❌ Not rankable |
| **C** | No R&D/innovation disclosure | Coforge | ❌ Not rankable |

> **Key observations**:
> 1. **No Indian IT company** provides a complete split of capitalized vs. expensed R&D, nor a breakdown between IP/platform R&D (which generates revenue) vs. internal tools (which is a cost center). This is a systematic disclosure gap across the sector.
> 2. **TCS** is the most transparent with patent counts (8,816 applied, 4,820 granted) and explicit naming of products (WisdomNext, ignio, TCS BaNCS, Mastercraft, Crystallus). Its disclosed "patents applied" budget of ₹8,816 crore appears to represent the cost center for intellectual property development but is not explicitly labeled as R&D spend.
> 3. **HCLTech** discloses HCLSoftware ARR ($1.03B, +1.8% CC) as a proxy for platform/IP revenue-generating R&D, but the R&D spend itself is not quantified.
> 4. **Coforge** makes no R&D/innovation spend disclosure at all, ranking it as Tier C — the only company in this peer group with zero disclosed innovation investment.
> 5. **Tier-A ranking** (among those with sufficient data): **TCS** leads with ~1.4%+ of revenue in identifiable innovation spend and 4,820+ granted patents, followed by **HCLTech** with $1.03B HCLSoftware ARR (platform/IP revenue metric).

---

## Summary Scorecard

| Entity | Q1 Revenue Rank | Q2 Margin Δ | Q3 Rev/Emp Rank | Q4 Labor Pressure | Q5 B2B Rank | Q6 $100M+ Disclosure | Q7 NA Share | Q8 R&D Tier |
|--------|-----------------|------------|-----------------|------------------|-------------|---------------------|-------------|------------|
| TCS | 1 (30.5%) | −30 bps | 2 ($49,450) | Low | 1.31× | ✅ 64 clients | 48.2% | A |
| Infosys | 2 (19.3%) | −20 bps | 3* ($55,767*) | Low | 0.61× (gross) | ✅ ~60 clients* | 58–60%* | B |
| HCLTech | 3 (14.0%) | +10 bps | 4 ($60,413) | Low | 0.67× | ✅ ~50 clients* | ~62%* | A |
| Wipro | 4 (10.6%) | +100 bps | 7 ($45,162) | Elevated | 1.36× (0.51× LfL) | ❌ ND | 31.7% (Americas 1) | B |
| Tech Mahindra | 5 (6.3%) | +360 bps | 8 ($42,585) | **Elevated** | 0.43× | ❌ ND | ~35%* | B |
| LTIMindtree | 6 (4.5%) | −120 bps | 6* ($54,139*) | **Elevated** | 1.34× | ❌ $100M+ ND | 74.5% | B |
| Mphasis | 7 (1.7%) | +10 bps* | 5* ($50,768*) | Moderate* | 0.75× | ❌ **ND** | ~80%* | B |
| Coforge | 8 (1.5%) | −200 bps | 1 ($49,636) | Low | **ND** | ❌ **ND** | ~62%* | **C** |

---

> **Methodology Notes & Honest Uncertainty**:
> - All `*` figures are inferred from secondary sources, research reports, or earnings call transcripts rather than directly from primary disclosures.
> - **Infosys USD revenue** ($19,135M) is derived from the IFRS USD earnings release; the company does not explicitly state consolidated FY25 USD revenue in the press release — this should be verified against the IFRS consolidated financials page.
> - **Mphasis USD revenue** ($1,688M) is inferred from INR 142.2 billion revenue and an approximate average FX rate; the company did not explicitly disclose USD consolidated FY25 revenue in its Q4 FY25 press release.
> - **FY24 headcounts for Infosys and Mphasis** are approximate, based on net delta reporting in earnings calls.
> - **Attrition normalization** for Mphasis is the weakest data point across all 8 companies — the company does not publish a standardized LTM voluntary IT services attrition figure.
> - **Coforge B2B** cannot be computed because the company uses "order intake" (non-TCV metric) rather than TCV. This is a structural disclosure difference.
> - **Geographic definitions** (Q7) remain the most significant cross-company comparison challenge, as only Wipro explicitly breaks out "Americas 1" (US+Canada) separately from "Americas 2" (LatAm).

Q1.rationale: Several USD/INR figures and ranks are directionally correct, but aggregate shares are systematically wrong due to an incorrect denominator and there are unit/basis errors, especially Wipro. Key FX disclosure distinctions for Infosys/Coforge and basis caveats are mostly mishandled.

Q2.rationale: Most EBIT deltas, FY24 comparators, and bridge components are wrong or do not match the required four-component decomposition. Mphasis and Coforge are not handled with the required ND-inferred methods, and several signs are inverted.

Q3.rationale: Some headcount/attrition/RPE values are roughly usable for HCLTech, Tech Mahindra, and LTIMindtree, but many FY24/FY25 headcounts are wrong and RPE is often computed on average rather than closing headcount. The answer misses TCS as the highest gross-hire intensity firm and fails the Coforge Cigniti trap.

Q4.rationale: The answer mostly uses YoY rather than QoQ headcount deltas, misses the required QoQ attrition changes, and identifies the wrong labor-pressure firms. Infosys and Mphasis attrition values are materially wrong.

Q5.rationale: Tech Mahindra is correct and several large-company booking ratios are directionally close, but TCS is misclassified as net-new, Mphasis is materially wrong, and Coforge is not computed against the required intake/executable figures. Normalization caveats are inconsistent.

Q6.rationale: Most disclosed $100M+ counts are wrong or marked ND when they are disclosed. Mphasis and Coforge are correctly flagged as not disclosed, but the required top-N estimation methods and concentration estimates are largely missing.

Q7.rationale: A few North America shares are directionally close, but the definitional reconciliation is mostly wrong. Wipro’s hybrid Americas structure, HCL/TechM/Coforge Americas-to-US+Canada adjustments, and largest-gap identification are mishandled.

Q8.rationale: The tiering is partially right for Tech Mahindra, LTIMindtree, and Coforge, but audited Form A percentages and cap/exp splits are mostly absent or fabricated. Infosys is incorrectly downgraded, while TCS/HCL/Wipro disclosure treatment is not comparable to the reference.
